René Descartes on certainty

René Descartes (1596–1650) approaches certainty within Rationalism. The cogito identifies thinking as indubitable; he distinguished thinking substance from extended substance and defended clear and distinct ideas. Systematically, the teaching links method, mind, mathematics into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets certainty most directly—useful for searches such as “rené descartes quotes on certainty.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the René Descartes thinker page for biography and to the certainty theme for other voices on the same question.
